title: Nasdaq IV Rank Says 42. Implied Vol Is Only 20. That Gap Matters.
speaker: Jonathan Haas (Altius Capital), guest

macro_themes.view: Inflation report pushed yields, dollar and oil up together, which is what has been undoing the market.
Nasdaq IV ~20 and VIX ~15.8 in contango look too quiet for a fast market with earnings, Fed and election ahead; stay small and hedge with butterflies/calendars.
Tech keeps pricing power while consumer staples weaken; consumer weakness could steepen the curve with long bonds rallying.

calls.reason: Bonds sold off on CPI but stopped right at the moving average, suggesting the week's selling exhaustion is playing out; consumer weakness could bring long bonds back up. Likes selling OTM puts (98/99 strikes).
calls.quote: maybe this exhaustion that we saw over the over the last sort of week or so is maybe playing through now

calls.reason: After two weeks of harvest-driven selling, moves are getting smaller with larger wicks; plays both sides of the recent range with calendars/diagonals plus downside butterfly.
calls.quote: there's an interesting opportunity to play both sides on that

notes: Transcript content (upcoming election, Fed expected) reads like an older 2024 segment; date taken from listing. ZB/ZS are not in the canonical list; kept raw futures symbols (ZB bias is on bond price, i.e. bearish yields). Host cited VIX 15.81 and Nasdaq IVR 42/IV 20 without a directional call.
